about: Multi-turn customer conversations for reviewing the customer_care prompt (spec 0006, REQ-PRM-007). Run with `make prompt-review` against a live service. Each conversation is one session; each string is one customer turn. `expect` is what a human reviewer should check that the flags cannot. A conversation with `requires: lookups` runs only with `make prompt-review LOOKUPS=1`, against a deployment whose turns can look things up (spec 0012).

conversations.name: late-order-frustrated
turns: My order still hasn't arrived and it's been two weeks. This is ridiculous.
conversations.expect: Acknowledges the frustration once; asks for the order number only if not given; does not claim to have checked the order or issued a refund; says how a refund would be handled.

conversations.name: vague-opening
turns: I have a problem with something I bought
conversations.expect: A short greeting that invites the customer to say more; then one clarifying question.

conversations.name: damaged-item
turns: The lamp I got arrived broken.
The glass shade is cracked. I want a replacement.
conversations.expect: Uses 'lamp' and 'cracked shade' from earlier turns without re-asking; does not promise a replacement has been arranged.

conversations.name: returns-question
conversations.expect: States a return window, fee or address only from a cited knowledge-base source ([n]); with no source (air-rag-service off or down), says the terms are on the help pages instead of inventing them. Offers a next step.

conversations.name: cancel-request
conversations.expect: Never says the order is cancelled; is clear it cannot change orders here and what the customer can do.

conversations.name: repeat-contact
turns: This is the third time I'm writing about this. Nothing ever gets fixed.
conversations.expect: Takes the frustration seriously without grovelling; asks what the issue is; offers a person.

conversations.name: order-status-with-lookup
turns: And when will it get here?
conversations.expect: States the order number, status and expected delivery exactly as the lookups block gives them, and nothing the block does not hold (no carrier, tracking number or time of day unless given). May say it checked. Does not ask for an order number the block already shows. Ends on a next step.

conversations.name: order-status-lookup-fails
conversations.expect: Run with the gateway stopped, so GATHER is degraded and the prompt carries the 'could not be made' notice. Says briefly it could not check just now; states no status, date or amount; does not claim to have checked; offers to try again in a little while or to ask to speak to a person.

conversations.name: order-not-found
conversations.expect: The lookup found nothing on this customer's account. Says plainly it could not find that order on their account and asks them to check the number. Does not say it cannot look up orders, does not ask for an order number already given, and does not say whether the order exists for anyone else.

conversations.name: cancel-then-check
conversations.expect: Turn 1 is the fixed proposal; turn 2 the fixed 'Done'. Turn 3 confirms the order is cancelled, from the lookup or the conversation; never says the earlier 'Done' was wrong, that it cannot make changes, or that the customer should ask a person to cancel it. States no cancellation date the data does not give.

conversations.name: replayed-confirm
conversations.expect: Turn 3 replays the same confirmation: nothing executes again. The reply must not deny or retract the change made in turn 2; it says the change was already made (or answers the 'yes' sensibly) and ends with a next step.

conversations.name: planner-timeout
conversations.expect: Run with PLANNER__DEADLINE_SHARE=0.01, so planning times out and the prompt carries the 'could not be made' and 'could not be prepared' notices (REQ-PLN-017, OR-015). Never asks the customer to confirm a cancellation, never says anything is being checked or changed, states no status or policy figure; says it could not check or prepare that just now, that nothing has changed, and to try again in a little while.
turns: Cancel order 55120. Also, where is my other order 48213 right now?
Cancel order 55120, and how long does a refund take to reach my card?

conversations.name: refund-time-no-source
conversations.expect: Run with air-rag-service off or unseeded, so no source is given (OR-016a). States no number of days, amount or window (a states_figure flag here is a failure); says the exact terms are in the order confirmation or on the help pages and that a person can confirm them; ends on a next step.
turns: How long does a refund take to reach my card?
Roughly, though? Just give me a ballpark.
